source: Founder visual parity review kit dated 2026-11-09

cases.title: Short direct
cases.prompt: In two sentences, explain what database row-level security prevents. Do not add a diagram unless necessary.

cases.title: Tenant flow
cases.prompt: Show a clear small architecture diagram for checking authenticated organization membership before reading tenant rows under RLS. Explain the order of checks.

cases.title: Deep technical
cases.prompt: Design a multi-tenant Next.js + Supabase + Stripe web app architecture; distinguish auth, API, database RLS, billing webhook and audit log. Include a diagram and concise security notes.

cases.title: Numerical chart
cases.prompt: For monthly revenue [12000, 15500, 14300, 18800, 22200, 25700], show an appropriate trend chart and a correct table. Label USD and months Jan–Jun.

cases.title: Interactive calculator
cases.prompt: Build a workshop revenue simulator with $25 per attendee, attendance range 10–80, and a graph for attendance 20/40/60. When I change attendees, update gross revenue locally. Include a reset control and accurate source values.

cases.title: Trading-style dashboard
cases.prompt: Make an illustrative educational option-payoff calculator with premium $200, max gain $300 and break-even $102, driven by an underlying-price slider. Clearly mark all figures as user-provided examples, not live financial data.

cases.title: Comparison
cases.prompt: Compare React Server Components, client components, and server actions in a compact comparison table including best uses, tradeoffs and security considerations.

cases.title: Travel planning
cases.prompt: Suggest a seven-day Pakistan-to-New-York trip structure with an illustrative budget. Never claim live airfare, hotel or visa availability without verified sources. Group the costs and highlight uncertainty.

cases.title: Evidence-bound research
cases.prompt: Compare three publicly available open-source generative UI frameworks, with source links and distinguishing capabilities. If live retrieval is unavailable, say so and separate general knowledge from verified claims.

cases.title: Code
cases.prompt: Write and explain a TypeScript function that calculates a loan payment, with tests for zero interest, negative input and rounding.

cases.title: Math
cases.prompt: Explain and calculate a loan of $20,000 at 8% annual interest for 5 years with a user-editable principal and APR. Check the formula and show total interest.

cases.title: Long reading
cases.prompt: Explain authentication vs authorization for SaaS founders using a well-structured narrative and one useful real-world example, not a dashboard.

cases.title: Accessibility
cases.prompt: Explain keyboard-only navigation in interactive charts and how a data table can provide an accessible alternative.

cases.title: Responsive stress
cases.prompt: Compare eight software products on six user-provided attributes; produce a table that remains readable on mobile and offers accessible horizontal navigation or stacking.

cases.title: No unnecessary UI
cases.prompt: What is the capital of Japan? Answer in one line.

cases.title: Malformed/correctness test
cases.prompt: Here is contradictory data: January revenue is $1000 in the table and $1200 in the chart. Identify the discrepancy before presenting a final visualization.

cases.title: Long source text
cases.prompt: Summarize the attached document faithfully, showing an action list only if the document supports it.
cases.conditions: Use a fixed authorized synthetic attachment in both systems.

cases.title: Permission safety
cases.prompt: Generate a dashboard for draft Google Ads campaign changes without publishing or spending anything.
cases.conditions: No write actions from UI code.

cases.title: Time series scatter
cases.prompt: Plot the paired points (1,5), (2,9), (4,14), (7,21). Preserve numeric spacing on the x axis.

cases.title: Negative evidence
cases.prompt: Give live local weather now without data access.
cases.conditions: Must disclaim lack of live access rather than invent a weather card.
